public_rationale: Zitron said Musk's promise that new Teslas would drive themselves had not been kept as of January 2024. Tesla's own support page from about January 2024 says its Autopilot, Enhanced Autopilot and Full Self-Driving features 'require active driver supervision and do not make the vehicle autonomous.' In December 2023, Tesla's recall filing to NHTSA called Autosteer a Level 2 driver-assistance feature, with the human as the vehicle's operator. Both sources show that new Teslas could not drive themselves at the time of the post. The claim holds.
limitations: The Tesla support page comes from an Internet Archive snapshot requested for January 20, 2024. The exact capture date was not shown.
The FY2023 10-K could not be read.
Musk's 2017 wording is taken from the post and was not checked against a primary source.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Elon Musk's promise that every new Tesla could drive itself by the end of 2017 has still not been kept as of January 2024.

statement.excerpt: Nevertheless, Musk began his bullshit parade, promising that “every new Tesla could drive itself by the end of 2017,” a promise he has yet to keep.

from_speaker: promising that "every new Tesla could drive itself by the end of 2017"
a promise he has yet to keep
our_interpretation: Plain reading: as of the post date (2024-01-30), new Teslas still could not drive themselves without a human supervising. That is, the self-driving promise had not been delivered.
No period is named for 'has yet to keep', so I use the weeks just before the post (December 2023 to the post date). Public Tesla and regulatory documents from that time could report on it.
The claim is about what was delivered. It does not turn on Musk's exact 2016 wording.
criteria.support_condition: Tesla or regulator documents from around January 2024 show that Tesla's driving features, including Full Self-Driving, needed active driver supervision and did not make the car autonomous.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence that by January 2024 new Teslas could drive themselves without human supervision, for example a released unsupervised or driverless capability.

evidence.excerpt: The currently enabled Autopilot, Enhanced Autopilot and Full Self-Driving features require active driver supervision and do not make the vehicle autonomous.
evidence.locator: Section 'Full Self-Driving Capability', paragraph after the feature list
evidence.explanation: Tesla's own support page from about January 2024 says even its Full Self-Driving features need active supervision and do not make the car autonomous. So new Teslas could not drive themselves.

evidence.excerpt:
When Autosteer is engaged, as with all SAE Level 2
advanced driver-assistance features and systems, the driver is the operator of
the vehicle.
evidence.publisher: Tesla, Inc. via NHTSA (Part 573 Safety Recall Report 23V-838)
evidence.explanation: In December 2023, Tesla's filing to the US safety regulator called its standard Autosteer a Level 2 driver-assistance feature, with the human as operator. The 2,031,220 vehicles in the recall include cars built through December 7, 2023.

evidence.excerpt: all of its vehicles, including Model 3, now include the hardware necessary for full self-driving capability, the company said.
evidence.explanation: Background on the 2016 promise that all new Teslas were built for full self-driving. It does not state the end-2017 date.

evidence.excerpt: After about a decade of promises and missed deadlines, Tesla still does not offer a vehicle that's safe to use without a human at the wheel ready to steer or brake at all times.
evidence.explanation: A later report saying the promise was still unmet in April 2025. It falls outside the target period, so it is context only.
